clue.text: Singular swimming-stroke with a bad hand

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
the crawl is the front swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A lone swimmer's stroke is paired with clumsy handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand can mean handwriting, and untidy, illegible writing is a scribble of that kind.

clue.text: Gemstone -perhaps one re-set

indicators.note: a gem that is re-set is placed again, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A jeweller suggests a precious stone might be put in a new mounting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious blue gem, a kind of gemstone.

clue.text: Science in split? Declare null and void!

indicators.note: in places the science piece inside the split piece

parts.note: to rend is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: Science is divided, and a law is struck off the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or contract is to revoke it, making it null and void.

clue.text: Does one have trouble keeping watch with this carpal disorder?

definitions.text: Does one have trouble keeping watch with this carpal disorder?

parts.words: Does one have trouble keeping watch with this carpal disorder?
parts.note: a condition of the joint below the hand, where a timepiece is worn, would make a wristwatch hard to hold up

explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping watch' suggests a sentry, but the watch is worn on the wrist; this condition leaves the hand hanging limp from paralysis of the forearm muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medical condition in which the hand hangs limp at the joint, a carpal disorder.

clue.text: Bashful in spinal injuries unit?

explanation.surface: A shy patient is placed in a hospital department for back injuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy, hesitant people are called retiring in this sense; read as two words it is a hospital ward for back patients.

clue.text: Wantonly halts migration of these numbers

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly and without restraint, telling us the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flock's journey is recklessly brought to a stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wantonly' rearranges HALTS MIGRATION, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An antilogarithm is the number whose logarithm is a given value, so these are numbers in mathematics.

clue.text: One that surpasses, for the listener, a letter from overseas

indicators.note: says the clue phrase must be heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to cap something is to surpass it, so one who does so is a capper

explanation.surface: An overseas letter sounds like it comes from someone who outdoes everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent CAPPER sounds like the Greek letter; 'from overseas' means foreign, here Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Failure to retain seaman I trained

indicators.note: trained means schooled into new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor says he was taught, but nothing stuck in his memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the inability to keep things in mind.

clue.text: The Spanish gooseberry?

parts.note: a gooseberry is an unwanted third person with a couple, so the Spanish version is a chaperone in a Spanish household

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'gooseberry' is a third person tagging along with a couple; this is the older woman who chaperoned girls in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna was an older woman acting as chaperone to young women in Spanish families, playing the unwelcome third party.

clue.text: Deceased's name released as a safety measure

parts.note: a deceased person is a dead man, so the possessive gives dead man's
a handle is slang for a name or nickname

explanation.surface: A dead person's name is made public as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released' looks like news being published, but it is part of the definition: the driver's control that stops a train when let go.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead man's handle on a train or machine cuts power when the operator lets go, a safety device.

clue.text: Silent pet trained to be vicious

indicators.note: a trained animal has been reshaped, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiet household animal is schooled into being aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent can describe something harmful or malicious, a near synonym of nasty and destructive.

clue.text: Pound given to church, with some coppers

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A pound sterling goes into the church collection along with a few small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money beside 'coppers', but it is an animal enclosure; coppers are low-value bronze British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: British pennies are copper-coloured coins, so a handful of them are small change.

clue.text: One, having comp red outside, is elevated

indicators.note: one piece has another piece around its outside, so it sits within that other word
one piece has another piece around its outside, so it sits within that other word

parts.note: to compere a show is to host it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who has presented a show is raised up on high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having ... outside' puts I (one) within HOSTED (compered); the printed 'comp red' is the scan losing the letters of 'compered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoisted means raised or lifted up, the same as being elevated.

clue.text: Affair with Alison I abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, signalling these letters run riot

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man confesses to a reckless fling with a woman called Alison.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic relationship, which is what an affair is.

clue.text: Haggard horseman

explanation.surface: A gaunt, exhausted figure on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective, but it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, author of King Solomon's Mines, whose middle name gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer H. Rider Haggard carried this name before his surname, and a mounted person on horseback is one too.

clue.text: North African in a regal constitution

indicators.note: a constitution is how something is made up, so these letters are composed afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from North Africa has a kingly physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: IN A REGAL gives eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Algeria is a person from that North African nation.

clue.text: Carpet salesman over border — and moving!

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the salesman piece above the border piece

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: moving tells us the letters of the word and shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A rug seller crosses the frontier on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like a floor covering, but it is the verb meaning to scold; 'moving' rearranges AND into MAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for giving them a dressing-down, a formal rebuke.

clue.text: Old gag for a horse

explanation.surface: A tired joke is told about a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stale, overused joke is called this; it is also a reddish-brown horse.

clue.text: Toastmaster to hold up rosé that is drunk

parts.note: to prop something is to hold it up

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and unsteady, so these letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the accent is ignored

explanation.surface: The master of ceremonies steadies a glass of pink wine about to be downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like it describes the wine being swallowed, but it is the signal to scramble the letters of 'rosé', the accent counting for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who proposes a toast at a dinner is acting as the toastmaster.

clue.text: Wife once taking notes in costal architecture

parts.note: in Genesis Eve was made from Adam's rib, so rib is a playful old word for a wife
C, A, G and E are all musical notes

explanation.surface: A woman of old picks up musical notes within the structure of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'costal' means relating to the ribs, so costal architecture is the bony frame of the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony frame around the chest is made of ribs, the costal structure.

clue.text: Inexpensive fruit?

parts.note: read as a wordplay riddle: the word meaning inexpensive, with its letters reshuffled, yields a fruit

explanation.walkthrough: There is no printed anagram signal: the question mark asks you to rearrange CHEAP, the word for 'inexpensive', into a stone fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, downy stone fruit whose five letters are those of the word for low-priced.

clue.text: How like a primate, to copy love

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them
to like something is to be fond of it, a mild form of love

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how a monkey imitates affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling a monkey or ape means resembling a primate.

clue.text: Priest carried in a bicycle rickshaw

indicators.note: carried in says the letters are borne within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A clergyman is ferried about in a pedal-powered taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, such as a priest.

clue.text: Lamb after highball can be a bloomer!

indicators.note: after places the Lamb piece behind the highball piece

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high into the air
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A lamb follows a lofted ball, and somebody makes a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobelia is a garden plant grown for its flowers, so it blooms.

clue.text: Suggestion heard from Latvians formerly

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken and we write what is said

parts.note: let's, short for let us, is a way of making a suggestion

explanation.surface: A proposal comes, by rumour, from the Baltic people of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Letts is an older English name for the Latvian people.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen ts Eliot play!

indicators.note: play suggests letters moving freely and being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An audience is welcomed to a drama by the poet T S Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies and gentlemen' sounds like an address to an audience, but signs reading 'Ladies' and 'Gentlemen' are on public lavatory doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Public lavatories are labelled for each sex, so these two words name the facilities.

clue.text: Acknowledge sappers' performance

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, the army's sappers, are the RE
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: Engineers in the army are asked to applaud a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something, which shows you have noticed it.

clue.text: Doom of mother race

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a race of people can be a nation

explanation.surface: A mother's people face a terrible fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is eternal punishment, a condemnation to ruin like doom.

clue.text: Bishops in these roles never change colour

definitions.text: Bishops in these roles never change colour

parts.words: Bishops in these roles never change colour
parts.note: describes pieces on a chequered board, where a bishop moves only diagonally and so stays on one shade of square

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clergy who never blush or change robes; a chess bishop moves diagonally, so it stays on squares of one colour all game.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is one of the pieces of the board game, and it always remains on its starting square colour.

clue.text: Expected arrival of vet, and with treatment

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are handled and reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal doctor is due to turn up with medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is a coming or arrival, especially one long awaited.
